title: Advanced Ovarian Cancer
description: Assess with a gynecologic oncologist, choose primary or interval cytoreduction by the chance of complete resection, skip lymphadenectomy of normal nodes, and match maintenance to BRCA status.
objectives: Complete the initial assessment, including universal germline and somatic BRCA testing
Choose primary cytoreduction when complete resection is likely, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy when it is not
Confirm the histology before neoadjuvant chemotherapy and use a platinum–taxane doublet
Time interval cytoreduction, and know where HIPEC fits
Avoid systematic lymphadenectomy of normal nodes, and offer maintenance therapy

references.citation: Gaillard S, Lacchetti C, Armstrong DK, et al. Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy for Newly Diagnosed, Advanced Ovarian Cancer: ASCO Guideline Update. J Clin Oncol. 2025;43(7):868-891.
Harter P, Sehouli J, Lorusso D, et al. A Randomized Trial of Lymphadenectomy in Patients with Advanced Ovarian Neoplasms. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(9):822-832.

Kehoe S, Hook J, Nankivell M, et al. Primary chemotherapy versus primary surgery for newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer (CHORUS): an open-label, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial. Lancet. 2015;386(9990):249-257.
Moore K, Colombo N, Scambia G, et al. Maintenance Olaparib in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Advanced Ovarian Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(26):2495-2505.

start.text: A 63-year-old woman has 3 months of bloating and early satiety. Examination finds ascites and a pelvic mass. CA-125 is 1,840 U/mL, and CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows bilateral adnexal masses, an omental cake, and peritoneal nodules.

assess.text: Which belong in her initial assessment?

options.label: Evaluation by a gynecologic oncologist before any treatment
Germline and somatic BRCA1/2 testing now
Genetic testing only if she has a family history
Start chemotherapy now based on CT and CA-125 alone

assess.feedback: ASCO 2025: a gynecologic oncologist should evaluate every patient with suspected stage III–IV disease before therapy (strong). Assessment includes CA-125, CT of the abdomen and pelvis, and chest imaging, preferably CT (strong). Offer all patients germline and somatic BRCA1/2 testing at diagnosis, whatever the family history (strong). Before neoadjuvant chemotherapy, obtain histologic confirmation, preferably by core biopsy.

resectable.text: She is fit (ECOG 0), and the gynecologic oncologist, after diagnostic laparoscopy, judges complete cytoreduction likely with acceptable morbidity. Plan?

options.label: Primary cytoreductive surgery aiming for no visible residual disease
options.feedback: ASCO 2025 (conditional): for patients fit for surgery with a high likelihood of complete cytoreduction and acceptable morbidity, primary cytoreduction is recommended over neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Suitability depends on fitness, performance status, frailty, nutrition, and the surgical complexity required.

options.label: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for every stage III patient
options.feedback: ASCO 2025: neoadjuvant chemotherapy is for patients unlikely to be completely cytoreduced or at high perioperative risk. When a fit patient is likely to achieve complete cytoreduction, primary surgery is recommended. EORTC 55971 and CHORUS found neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-inferior, but JCOG0602 did not confirm this.

nodes.text: She has complete macroscopic resection of all intra-abdominal disease. Her retroperitoneal nodes looked normal on CT and feel normal at surgery. What about the nodes?

options.label: Systematic pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy for staging
options.feedback: In LION, patients with complete resection and clinically normal nodes gained no survival from systematic lymphadenectomy (median overall survival 65.5 vs 69.2 months without). They had more repeat laparotomies (12.4% vs 6.5%) and higher 60-day mortality (3.1% vs 0.9%).

options.label: Leave the clinically normal nodes
options.feedback: In LION, systematic pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy after complete resection with clinically normal nodes did not improve overall survival (65.5 vs 69.2 months) or progression-free survival (25.5 months in both). It increased repeat laparotomy (12.4% vs 6.5%) and 60-day mortality (3.1% vs 0.9%).

unresectable.text: Laparoscopy and imaging show extensive disease on the small-bowel mesentery and around the porta hepatis. The gynecologic oncologist judges complete cytoreduction unlikely. Plan?

options.label: Primary surgery anyway, to remove as much tumor as possible
options.feedback: ASCO 2025 (strong): when a fit patient is unlikely to achieve complete cytoreduction, neoadjuvant chemotherapy is recommended over primary surgery. In CHORUS, primary chemotherapy was non-inferior for survival (median 24.1 vs 22.6 months), with fewer grade 3–4 postoperative complications (14% vs 24%) and fewer 28-day deaths.

options.label: Core biopsy to confirm the diagnosis, then platinum–taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy
options.feedback: ASCO 2025: when complete cytoreduction is unlikely, neoadjuvant chemotherapy is recommended over primary surgery (strong). Confirm invasive cancer histologically first, preferably by core biopsy. Use a platinum–taxane doublet, especially for high-grade serous or endometrioid cancer (strong); single-agent carboplatin gave worse survival in vulnerable older patients.

options.label: Single-agent carboplatin, to limit toxicity
options.feedback: ASCO 2025 (strong): use a platinum–taxane doublet for neoadjuvant chemotherapy, especially in high-grade serous disease. In a GINECO trial in vulnerable older patients, single-agent carboplatin was less active and gave significantly worse survival than the three-weekly doublet.

interval.text: After 3 cycles her CA-125 has fallen to 120 U/mL and CT shows a good response. She has stage III disease, good performance status, and normal renal function. What next?

options.label: Continue to 8 cycles of chemotherapy before considering surgery
options.feedback: ASCO 2025 (conditional): perform interval cytoreduction after 4 or fewer cycles in patients who respond or have stable disease. In a meta-analysis of 7,005 patients, survival was better with fewer cycles before interval surgery.

options.label: Interval cytoreduction now, discussing HIPEC at surgery
options.feedback: ASCO 2025: perform interval cytoreduction after 4 or fewer cycles for response or stable disease (conditional). For stage III disease with good performance status and renal function, HIPEC may be offered at interval surgery through shared decision-making (conditional). In OVHIPEC-1, median overall survival was 44.9 vs 33.3 months. Complete a total of six cycles afterward.

maintenance.text: She completes six cycles in total with a complete response. Her testing shows a germline BRCA1 mutation. What do you offer?

options.label: PARP-inhibitor maintenance, such as olaparib, plus genetic counseling
options.feedback: ASCO 2025 (strong): offer FDA-approved maintenance, such as a PARP inhibitor or bevacizumab, weighing benefit, adverse effects, and quality of life. In SOLO1, olaparib maintenance for BRCA-mutated disease after response to platinum cut the risk of progression or death by 70%; 60% vs 27% were progression-free at 3 years. Genetic counseling is recommended for anyone with a heritable variant.

options.label: Six more cycles of carboplatin–paclitaxel as consolidation
options.feedback: ASCO 2025: a total of six cycles is recommended. After that, offer approved maintenance, such as a PARP inhibitor (in SOLO1, 70% lower risk of progression or death with BRCA mutations) or bevacizumab, rather than more chemotherapy.

fail_sequence.text: Guideline Deviation: Treatment sequence off the evidence.

fail_lymphadenectomy.text: Complication: Morbidity from an unnecessary lymphadenectomy.

fail_maintenance.text: Guideline Deviation: Maintenance therapy not offered.

success.text: Case Complete: Cytoreduction sequenced by resectability, maintenance by BRCA status.
